title: This California river once carried thousands of salmon every year. A 1942 dam changed it forever, and scientists are still trying to bring them back
summary_full: Friant Dam construction in 1942 altered the San Joaquin River, impacting salmon populations.  A 2006 settlement agreement initiated restoration efforts for the river and its fish.  The program aims to reestablish spring-run Chinook salmon while managing water for agriculture.  Multiple agencies collaborate on scientific research and habitat improvements for the river.  Monitoring tracks progress and guides adjustments for long-term ecological recovery.
